decisions.rationale: The assertion concerns tunneling enabling electron penetration of a potential barrier, not enabling the electron itself as the target capability or process.
The shortage arises from quantity demanded exceeding quantity supplied; omitting quantity supplied removes an essential condition of the asserted causal relationship.
The requirement concerns quantum theory converging to classical limits, so the classical-limit side of the assertion is essential and is omitted from the edge.
RNA polymerase is a binding participant and DNA is the stated binding substrate; the gene location can remain contextual without changing this binding assertion.
The API component is explicitly one of the components separated by the modular order-processing service, so it is a part of that containing system.
The order-command-transfer symbol denotes the transfer event, not the destination or recipient; the asserted destination is the order component.
The amino acid is the item brought and the ribosome is the destination; transfer RNA can remain contextual to the item-to-destination relation.
The double-slit experiment is the stated setup producing the interference pattern, matching the cause-to-effect contract.
The assertion concerns tunneling enabling electron penetration in a light-switch context, not enabling a transistor; the proposed target is not the asserted enabled capability or process.
The assertion is a quantified prohibition on two electrons within an atom sharing a set of quantum numbers, which cannot be faithfully represented by a simple principle-to-electron edge.
